bull_bear.body:
- ~INR600 cr invested to acquire the two O&M portfolios (debt-funded; the ~INR40 cr "other income" is the return on that).
- Future FCF: first integrate acquisitions, then opportunistic acquisitions (≤10–20% of FCF), with dividend/buyback "in interest of shareholders" to be decided by Board post-consolidation.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Earnings quality:** large slice of EBITDA/other income is acquisition/debt-related and not-yet-consolidated operating profit — headline ~50% margin drops to ~45% ex that.
- **Timing risk:** FY27 INR600 cr depends on NCLT/EOI approvals landing for both acquired entities (final phases; 60–90 days).
- **Group execution credibility:** investors flagged repeated guidance misses at Inox Wind (MW→revenue guidance switch; INR5,000 cr → INR4,600 cr FY26 on ECS supply-chain/geopolitical delays, PSU payment delays).
- **Related-party concentration:** Inox Clean is the dominant future order source for the group — cycle/governance dependency.
- **Solar BESS substitution / FDRE battery focus** raised as a structural question for wind demand.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, defensive under pointed minority-shareholder pushback on value destruction and guidance misses; Devansh Jain emphasizes 4-yr value creation, "only Indian wind player that survived with zero haircut," renewable arm "valued north of $10bn." Combative ("don't hold us responsible for a world war"). FY27 75% growth framed as "conservative."
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Sector consolidation thesis: of 5 wind players, "2 allied, 3 bankrupt; we acquired 2 of the 3 bankrupt" — Inox Green is structurally cornering Indian wind O&M.
- INR700 cr accumulated-loss tax shield → near-100% cash conversion of FY27 EBITDA.
- Evacuation-infra demerger is the real ROE/ROCE lever (gross block + depreciation stripped out), not just operating growth.
- Inox Wind's pivot to 75–80% equipment supply (from 100% turnkey 24 months ago) indirectly de-risks Green's parent and working capital.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 'An Asset-light Growth-oriented Annuity Business Model' — 'Asset-light balance sheet post the demerger; Focus: Long-term contracts with steady cashflows'.
- Capital is being deployed inorganically: the portfolio figure includes 'the investments made to acquire ~ 6.5 GW of operational wind O&M portfolio of two companies', and management calls the Wind World transaction 'value accretive for shareholders'.
- The deck offers a forward earnings framing rather than a payout policy: 'Post completion of the acquisitions and consolidation of financials, Inox Green's consolidated EBITDA and PAT are expected to increase multifold.'
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Annuity cash-flow model — long-term O&M contracts with tenors of up to 25 years provide recurring revenue visibility, customer stickiness and high switching costs
- Synergistic group structure — as a subsidiary of Inox Wind Limited within the INOXGFL Group, the Company gets a captive pipeline of O&M mandates bundled with turbine supply contracts, plus access from Inox Wind, Inox Clean Energy, EPC and solar manufacturing
- Scale and pan-India reach — a 13+ GWp O&M portfolio with on-ground teams across India's key renewable energy corridors, enabling rapid response and reducing single-geography concentration
- Technology-driven maintenance — 24x7 centralised monitoring, SCADA-based analysis, predictive and preventive maintenance and a mobile O&M platform, with the SAP HANA transition operationally effective during FY26
- Demonstrated high machine availability of 96.5% in FY26, evidencing service reliability and execution discipline
- Asset-light business model with low capital intensity, sharpened further by the demerger of the power evacuation business into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited
- Over a decade of operational experience in renewable O&M across diverse geographies and operating conditions
- Proven inorganic execution — the Company emerged as successful bidder for Wind World (India) Limited's ~4.5 GW wind O&M portfolio through an NCLT-approved resolution process
- Lifecycle value creation through specialised offerings — WTG overhaul, refurbishment, booster sales, carbon credit-related services and life-extension solutions that expand share of wallet
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive pressures in renewable energy services — Intensifying competition within the renewable energy services sector may exert pressure on market share, pricing and profitability. Mitigated by differentiated value through predictive maintenance, operational excellence, technology-enabled service delivery and long-term customer relationships.
- Contract-related risk — delays, modifications, non-renewals or cancellations — Delays in project execution, contract modifications, non-renewals or cancellations may affect revenue visibility and growth prospects. This is structurally material because the entire business is an annuity model resting on a large number of long-term O&M contracts; the Company runs a centralised Revenue Assurance function for billing, contract compliance and collections monitoring precisely because of this.
- Regulatory and policy dependence — Changes in government policies, incentive structures, tariff mechanisms or renewable energy regulations may influence sector growth and investment activity. The Company's demand pipeline is directly tied to policy-driven renewable capacity addition (RPO trajectory, ISTS waivers, bidding trajectory), so a policy reversal would compress the addressable O&M pool.
- Geographic and single-activity concentration — Dependence on wind-rich regions may limit growth opportunities and expose operations to regional market dynamics. Structurally, the Company operates in a single reportable business segment (O&M services) and a single geographical segment — India only, with NIL exports and only domestic turnover — so it has no diversification cushion outside Indian renewable O&M. Mitigation is expansion into solar, hybrid, RTC/FDRE and BESS O&M across multiple corridors.
- Workforce availability and attrition — Shortages of skilled technical personnel and employee attrition may affect service quality, operational efficiency and business scalability. This is a live structural exposure — permanent-employee turnover was 33.15% in FY2025-26 (44.51% in FY2024-25) — in a business whose service quality depends on on-ground technicians across dispersed sites.
- Technological obsolescence — Rapid technological advancements may alter operating requirements and create competitive advantages for market participants with superior capabilities. The Company is responding with investment in 24x7 centralised asset monitoring, advanced SCADA analytics, mobile-enabled O&M management platforms and SAP HANA implementation.
- Third-party and related-party transaction exposure — Business relationships with vendors, contractors and other external stakeholders may expose the Company to operational, commercial and compliance-related risks. Structurally amplified by high related-party concentration — related parties accounted for 25.09% of sales and 16.15% of purchases in FY2025-26, and 100% of both loans and advances given and investments made.
- Integration and execution risk on acquisition-led scale-up — The growth strategy leans heavily on inorganic expansion — the Wind World India Limited approximately 4.5 GW O&M acquisition pending completion in Q2 FY27, and a stated target of approximately 20 GW portfolio within two years. Management explicitly flags forward-looking statements on growth plans, portfolio targets and strategic objectives as not guarantees of future performance, with actual results able to differ materially.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as a 'Subsidiary of IWL; India's leading renewable O&M services player with ~13.3 GWp of assets under management. Inox Green is India's only listed pure-play renewable O&M service company.'
- The moat claimed is group inter-play: Inox Wind (one of India's largest wind turbine manufacturing players) has a 'Robust orderbook of ~4.4 GW as on July'26', and group IPP platform Inox Clean targets 3 GW+ annual capacity addition of which '~20% - 30% ... is expected to be wind', giving Inox Green 'multi-year multi-GW portfolio growth'.
- Sponsor backing is framed as 'Strong support from sponsor, INOXGFL Group, a USD 16 bn Indian conglomerate with deep interests across chemicals and renewables' (group size stated as on June 30, 2026 at INR:USD Rs. 96).

business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] The Wind World India (erstwhile Enercon India) ~4.5 GW wind O&M portfolio 'generated revenue of Rs. 580 crore in FY26 and benefits from contracted annual price escalation of approximately 5%'; its client base includes the Tata Group, ReNew, Greenko Group, Apraava Energy and Hindustan Zinc, with assets across Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh.
- [Demerger] 'Demerger of the power evacuation business has been completed as on August 1 2026 (being the record date)'; the deck also flags '# Restatement of financials due to discontinued operations' against the Q1 FY26 comparatives.
- [Group structure] INOXGFL Group has a legacy of over nine decades with three listed entities, spanning fluoropolymers and fluorochemicals (Gujarat Fluorochemicals, largest PTFE/fluoropolymer manufacturer in India), battery chemicals, wind turbines (Inox Wind: 2MW, 3MW and upcoming 4MW class WTGs), EPC (IRSL, formerly Resco Global), renewable O&M (IGESL), and solar cells & modules; Inox Solar targets 11 GW of solar cell & module manufacturing capacity across India and the USA and Inox Neo targets 14 GW of hybrid RE capacity by FY29.
- [Sector backdrop] The deck cites India's RE capacity (ex-large hydro) at ~237 GW as of Jun'26 with 13.9 GW added in Q1 FY27; of 9.34 GW awarded through tenders in Q1 FY27, 4.55 GW (49%) was wind/Hybrid/FDRE; India targets 500 GW/1,800 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030/2047; onshore wind potential is put at 695 GW at 120m hub height and 1,164 GW at 150m hub height, with 8-10 GW annual wind installations expected in the near term.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Inox Green provides long-term operations and maintenance services for Wind Turbine Generators, solar projects, hybrid/RTC/FDRE assets and battery energy storage systems, along with the associated common infrastructure required for efficient power evacuation. Services span preventive and predictive maintenance, corrective maintenance, condition monitoring, remote asset surveillance, fault diagnosis, breakdown management, spare parts planning, performance optimisation and site management. Customers include Independent Power Producers, public sector power utilities, corporate entities, commercial establishments and retail energy consumers, served under multi-year annuity contracts with tenors of up to 25 years.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Inox Green is an asset-light services business with no manufacturing plants; its expansion is measured in renewable O&M portfolio rather than physical capex. During FY26 the Company's total renewable O&M portfolio increased to over 13 GWp — approximately 13.3 GWp of wind and solar assets as on 31 March 2026, comprising about 10.3 GW of wind and about 3.0 GWp of solar, plus approximately 600 MW of wind O&M capacity that the Company also controls — spread across 11 states. The solar O&M portfolio was built from a negligible base at the start of FY26 to approximately 3 GWp within the year, driven by multiple contract wins including a significant project at Bhadla Solar Park, marking strategic diversification beyond wind into solar, hybrid and BESS O&M. The principal inorganic step was the Company emerging as the successful bidder for Wind World (India) Limited's approximately 4.5 GW wind O&M portfolio through an NCLT-approved resolution process; approval from the Hon'ble NCLT, Ahmedabad was received subsequent to year-end and transaction completion is expected in Q2 FY27, which management expects to strengthen scale, customer access and operational depth across key wind-rich states. Management has set a target of expanding the renewable O&M portfolio to approximately 20 GW over the next two years through a balanced mix of organic growth and selective acquisitions. Organic expansion is anchored on Inox Wind Limited's order book of approximately 4.4 GW as on July 2026, where O&M is typically bundled with turbine supply, and on group company Inox Clean Energy's targets of 10 GW of installed renewable capacity and 11 GW of module manufacturing capacity by FY28, which create a growing captive O&M pipeline. Further inorganic headroom is estimated at approximately 10 GW of Indian wind O&M assets owned by inactive, distressed or under-serviced operators. Other FY26 developments include a Letter of Award from NLC India Limited for 200 MW and an MOU with Inox Clean Energy or its subsidiaries. On the platform side, the Company completed its transition to SAP HANA, which became operationally effective during FY26, alongside 24x7 centralised monitoring, SCADA-based diagnostics and a mobile-based O&M management platform. The demerger of the power evacuation business into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited, effective 4 May 2026 and completed as on 1 August 2026, further sharpened the asset-light, capital-efficient structure. The Company reported NIL R&D and NIL capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts in both the current and previous financial years.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Every renewable asset commissioned today creates a decades-long requirement for efficient operations and maintenance, so each new gigawatt commissioned adds to the long-term serviceable asset pool
- India added a record 55.3 GW of non-fossil capacity in FY2025-26, taking total non-fossil installed capacity to 283 GW, translating directly into a rapidly expanding base of assets requiring long-term professional O&M services
- India's cumulative installed wind capacity crossed 56 GW as of 31 March 2026 following a record annual addition of 6.05 GW, with targets to reach 100 GW of wind capacity by 2030 and 156 GW by 2036
- India's installed solar capacity reached 150.26 GW as of March 2026 with a record 44.6 GW added in FY26; solar capacity is projected to reach approximately 509 GW by FY2035-36, so solar O&M is expected to surpass wind in scale
- India's target of 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, supported by rising Renewable Purchase Obligations expected to reach 43.33% by FY2030 and ISTS charge waivers, provides visibility for future capacity additions and sustained O&M demand
- The renewable landscape is evolving from standalone wind and solar towards wind-solar hybrid, Round-the-Clock and Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy projects, creating opportunities for specialised multi-technology O&M providers
- India has 29.28 GW of wind projects and another 19.00 GW of hybrid projects under construction as on 31 March 2026, adding to the future O&M opportunity
- Wind turbines are capital-intensive assets where unplanned breakdowns cause significant repair costs and lost generation, while dust, heat and component wear progressively degrade solar panel efficiency — both driving demand for professional O&M
- India's solar O&M market is approaching an inflection point, driven by a rapidly expanding installed base, uneven service quality and a growing shift towards professional, technology-driven operators
- Battery energy storage is emerging as an asset class that broadens the scope of integrated asset management, with India expected to require 208 GWh of BESS capacity by 2030 and 35.8 GWh already under construction
- Green hydrogen (National Green Hydrogen Mission target of 5 MMT annual production by 2030) and a projected fivefold increase in India's data centre capacity by 2030 are emerging new demand vectors for renewable assets requiring O&M support
- Growth in the O&M portfolio, consistently high asset availability and increasing contribution from value-added services lifted profitability, while the annuity-led model and technology-enabled platform reinforced earnings quality and resilience
- Customers across the renewable energy sector are increasingly looking for strong, credible and Indian O&M service providers
- The Indian wind O&M market presents an estimated opportunity of approximately 10 GW from assets owned by inactive, distressed or under-serviced operators, and a few renewable O&M players are willing to divest stakes for strategic reasons
- MNRE has prescribed an annual bidding trajectory of 50 GW renewable capacity until FY2028, with at least 10 GW per annum reserved for wind projects
- Globally, wind O&M market size is estimated to grow from USD 46.20 billion in 2025 to USD 95.48 billion in 2034, supported by an ageing turbine fleet, harsher operating environments and larger, more complex turbine platforms
- O&M opportunities linked to Inox Wind Limited's order book of approximately 4.4 GW as on July 2026, where O&M services are typically bundled with turbine supply contracts
- Inox Clean Energy is targeting 10 GW of installed renewable energy capacity by FY28 and 11 GW of module manufacturing capacity by FY28, creating a growing captive O&M pipeline
- Wind World India Limited O&M acquisition expected to add approximately 4.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets, with completion expected in Q2 FY27
- Estimated inorganic opportunity of approximately 10 GW in the Indian wind O&M market from assets owned by inactive, distressed or under-serviced operators
- Letter of Award from NLC India Limited for 200 MW and an MOU with Inox Clean Energy or its subsidiaries signed during FY26
- Long-term O&M contracts with tenors of up to 25 years underpin recurring revenue visibility

open.item: The Company carries an estimated capital commitment for setting up wind farm projects awarded by SECI, unchanged from the previous year.
Completion of the Wind World India Limited O&M acquisition, adding approximately 4.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets, is expected in Q2 FY27.
The Company targets expanding its renewable energy O&M portfolio to approximately 20 GW over the next two years.
The Company expects a growing captive O&M pipeline as group company Inox Clean Energy targets 10 GW of installed renewable capacity and 11 GW of module manufacturing capacity by FY28.

The Company is upgrading its technology backbone with SCADA-based real-time monitoring and a SAP HANA implementation, which became operationally effective during FY26, with further upgradation underway.

drhp.business: Inox Green provides long-term operations and maintenance services for Wind Turbine Generators, solar projects, hybrid/RTC/FDRE assets and battery energy storage systems, along with the associated common infrastructure required for efficient power evacuation. Services span preventive and predictive maintenance, corrective maintenance, condition monitoring, remote asset surveillance, fault diagnosis, breakdown management, spare parts planning, performance optimisation and site management. risks.note: Intensifying competition within the renewable energy services sector may exert pressure on market share, pricing and profitability. Mitigated by differentiated value through predictive maintenance, operational excellence, technology-enabled service delivery and long-term customer relationships.
risks.risk: Competitive pressures in renewable energy services

risks.note: Delays in project execution, contract modifications, non-renewals or cancellations may affect revenue visibility and growth prospects. This is structurally material because the entire business is an annuity model resting on a large number of long-term O&M contracts; the Company runs a centralised Revenue Assurance function for billing, contract compliance and collections monitoring precisely because of this.
risks.risk: Contract-related risk — delays, modifications, non-renewals or cancellations

risks.note: Changes in government policies, incentive structures, tariff mechanisms or renewable energy regulations may influence sector growth and investment activity. The Company's demand pipeline is directly tied to policy-driven renewable capacity addition (RPO trajectory, ISTS waivers, bidding trajectory), so a policy reversal would compress the addressable O&M pool.

Dependence on wind-rich regions may limit growth opportunities and expose operations to regional market dynamics. Structurally, the Company operates in a single reportable business segment (O&M services) and a single geographical segment — India only, with NIL exports and only domestic turnover — so it has no diversification cushion outside Indian renewable O&M. Mitigation is expansion into solar, hybrid, RTC/FDRE and BESS O&M across multiple corridors.

Shortages of skilled technical personnel and employee attrition may affect service quality, operational efficiency and business scalability. This is a live structural exposure — permanent-employee turnover was 33.15% in FY2025-26 (44.51% in FY2024-25) — in a business whose service quality depends on on-ground technicians across dispersed sites.

Rapid technological advancements may alter operating requirements and create competitive advantages for market participants with superior capabilities. The Company is responding with investment in 24x7 centralised asset monitoring, advanced SCADA analytics, mobile-enabled O&M management platforms and SAP HANA implementation.

Business relationships with vendors, contractors and other external stakeholders may expose the Company to operational, commercial and compliance-related risks. Structurally amplified by high related-party concentration — related parties accounted for 25.09% of sales and 16.15% of purchases in FY2025-26, and 100% of both loans and advances given and investments made.

The growth strategy leans heavily on inorganic expansion — the Wind World India Limited approximately 4.5 GW O&M acquisition pending completion in Q2 FY27, and a stated target of approximately 20 GW portfolio within two years. Management explicitly flags forward-looking statements on growth plans, portfolio targets and strategic objectives as not guarantees of future performance, with actual results able to differ materially.
